It covers three axes: (i) physical access to energy sources, measured, for example, by the existence of a connection to the National Interconnected System (SIN); (ii) possession of equipment, such as television, refrigerator, freezer and internet access; and (iii) accessibility, or the ability to pay for energy use, measured by the weight of energy expenses in the total household expenses. In the article, the Multidimensional Energy Poverty Index (MEPI) was calculated by state, differentiating between urban and rural populations. In AdaptaBrasil MCTI, in order to arrive at a single value for each state, the indicator was weighted by urban and rural populations.

This indicator measures dependence on large-scale irrigation, focusing on the characteristics of producers and agricultural establishments. It is calculated by multiplying the proportion of agricultural land using large-scale irrigation by a weight reflecting its regional importance in relation to drought threats. The proportion of irrigated land is based on the ratio of water used in irrigated agriculture to total water consumption, and the ratio of irrigated land using surface or sprinkler systems to total cultivated land. Water data comes from the 2017 Water Demand report by the National Water Agency (ANA), and irrigation data comes from the 2017 Agricultural Census by IBGE. Both are analyzed at the municipal level.
